title: WPMS/1682/2021 of NASEEM AHMAD Vs UTTARAKHAND POWER CORPORATION

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1682 of 2021
Naseem Ahmad .....Petitioner
Versus
Uttarakhand Power Corporation and others .... Respondents
Present :-
Mr. B.D. Pande, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal, Advocate for the respondents.

Dated: 24th September, 2021
JUDGEMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The brief facts, which engages consideration in the
present Writ Petition, are that in terms of the e-tendering
specifications No. 21/SE (MM)/2020-21, the bids were invited by the
respondents for the purposes of a sale of steel scrap Tank / Plate / GI
Wires/ Galvanized Scrape, etc.
2. The petitioner submitted that he responded to the said
invitation of bids, and in pursuance to the response given by the
petitioner, the bids were opened on 27th March, 2021, and
accordingly, the price bid was opened on 23rd April, 2021. On the
culmination of the bidding process, as referred above, the petitioner
was determined to be eligible and was held to be the highest bidders,
he was considered and a sale letter dated 28th June, 2021, was also
executed in his favour, whereby, an expression of letter of intent, was
issued to the petitioner offering him to accept the offer of deposit, as a
pre-condition for the purposes of executing the contract by depositing
a sum of Rs.1,79,19,430/-.
3. The petitioner submitted that on account of the financial
crisis, which was prevailing due to Covid-19 pandemic situation, he

2
was able to collect only part of the amount and deposit the same
before the respondents, to the tune of Rs.60 lacs, but the remaining
amount could not be deposited and, hence, he has sought for the
second relief, that the balance amount may be permitted to be
deposited by him in instalments. He further submits that, when the
request made by the petitioner for depositing the balance amount was
not acceded to, by the respondents, he represented his case before the
respondents on 14th July, 2021, but the same was not accepted by
them despite of its reiteration made on 16th July, 2021, and 9th August,
2021. As a consequence of the non response of the aforesaid letter,
and coupled with the fact that the petitioner had not deposited the
amount as directed by the respondents in pursuance to the sale letter
which was issued by them on 28th June, 2021, the respondents had
proceeded to pass the impugned order No. 607/SE (MM)/21/2020-
2021 dated 13th August, 2021, by virtue of which, the security amount
deposited by the petitioner was forfeited and he was further de-barred
from participating in the future tendering process for a period of two
years. It is this order dated 23.08.2021, which has been put to
challenge by the petitioner, with the simultaneous relief for a writ of
mandamus to accept the balance, amount in two or three equal
installments, and consequently to execute the contract.
4. Initially, when the Writ Petition had filed the Writ
Petition, the complete bidding documents was not appended, hence
this Court vide its order dated 09.09.2021, directed the petitioner to
place on record, the entire bidding documents and the same has been
submitted by the petitioner along with the supplementary affidavit,
which was filed on 19th September, 2021.
5. If the terms of the bidding document, particularly, the
Special Conditions of the Contract as provided in annexure-B to the
terms of the bidding document, in fact, the right of forfeiture and
black-listing has been the rights, which were reserved with the

3
employer as per Clause 6 of the Special Conditions of the Contract,
which is extracted hereunder :-
"6. The successful tenderer will have to deposit required
amount (including taxes) within 15 days from date of sale order
or as stated by UPCL. If the amount shall not be deposited
within stipulated period then Earnest Money of the firm will be
forfeited by the UPCL and the firm shall treated as debarred
for future tender of scrap sale for one year which can be
increased/decreased by competent UPCL Committee. In case
of non-payment after due date, UPCL reserve full right to take
decision regarding forfeitment of earnest money and black
listing of firm without assigning any reasons. No separate
notice etc. is required after due date of payment."
6. It was, while exercising the powers vested with them
under Clause 6 of annexure-B, to the Special Conditions of the
Contract, this impugned order dated 13.08.2021, has been passed
against the petitioner.
7. The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that
under an identical circumstance, though in relation to a different
contracting procedure which was resorted to by the respondents, way
back in 2018, other Writ Petitions were preferred before this Court
and there an interim order was granted, hence, an identical treatment
has to be judicially extended to the petitioner.
8. This Court is not in agreement with the arguments, which
have been extended by the learned counsel for the petitioner for the
reason being that :-
i. The interim orders passed, do not have any binding
effect on the Coordinate Benches, as it is not a ratio laid down
on merit consideration, but rather an interim arrangement made,
during the pendency of the lis.
ii. The interim orders, which were passed earlier, were in
relation to a different set of works and as a consequence of the
invitation of bid way back in 2017 and 2018 and the same
principles or analogy cannot be attracted to be borrowed in the

4
present Writ Petition, particularly, when the rights of the
employer were reserved under Clause 6 of the terms of the
contract.
9. It is not in dispute that a sale letter was already executed
in favour of the petitioner and in furtherance thereto, he has also
partially deposited the amount of Rs.60 lacs, for the purposes of
enabling the respondents to execute the contract. But as soon as the
expression of issuance of the sale letter after the petitioner being
determined as L1, has been communicated to the petitioner and he has
responded to the same, any default committed by him thereafter in
making the deposit in compliance of the sale letter issued in favour of
the petitioner by the respondents on 28th June, 2021, will fall to be
within the ambit of Clause 38 of the General Conditions of the
Contract, which provides for a Grievance Redressal Forum, as it
contemplates that if any dispute or difference arises between the
contractor, the same would be referable to an Arbitrator as provided
therein. Clause 38 is extracted hereunder :-
"38. If any dispute difference or controversy shall at
any time arise between the contractors on the one hand and the
UPCL and the Engineer of the contract on the other touching
the contract, or as to the true construction. Meaning and intent
or any part or condition of the same or as to the manner of
execution. Or as to the quality or description of the payment for
the same or as to the true intent, meaning, interpretation
construction or effect of the clauses of the contract,
specifications or drawing or any of them, or as to any thing to
be done committed or suffered in pursuance of the contract or
specification, or as in the mode of carrying the contract into
effect, or as to the breach or alleged breach, of the contract, or
as to any claims on account of such breach or alleged breach,
or as to obviation or compensating for the commission of any
such breach or alleged breach, or as the obviation or
compensating for the commission of any such breach, or as to
and whether before or during the progress or after the
completion of the Contract, such question difference or dispute
shall be referred for adjudication to the chairman, UPCL or to
any other person nominated by him in this behalf and his
decision in writing shall be final, binding and conclusive. This
submission shall be deemed to be a submission to arbitration

5
within the meaning of the Indian Arbitration Act 1940 or any
statutory modification thereof. The arbitrator may from time to
time with consent of the parties enlarge the time for making and
publishing the award.
Upon every or any such reference the costs of an
incidental to the reference and awards respectively shall be at
the discretion of the arbitrator, who shall be competent to
determine the amount thereof or direct the same to be taxed as
between solicitor client or as between party and party, and to
direct by whom and to whom and in what manner the same
shall be borne and paid.
Work under the contract shall, if reasonably possible,
continue during the arbitration proceedings no payments due
or payable by the Board shall be withheld on account of such
proceedings. In case of refusal/neglect by such nominee,
Chairman UPCL may nominate another person in his place.
Any action taken or proceedings initiated on any of the
terms of this agreement shall be only in the Court of Competent
jurisdiction under the High court of judicature at Nainital."
10. In exception, to the implications of Clause 38, the
learned counsel for the petitioner submitted, that mere issuance of the
sale letter may not amount to be a culmination of a right by execution
of the contract in order to attract the Clause 38. This Court after
having scrutinized the covonents of Clause 38 of the General
Conditions of the Contract, in fact, its invocation has also been
protected to be made applicable, with regard to the manner which is
resorted to by the parties to the bidding procedure, ultimately resulting
to the culmination of the contract. But, here, in this case since there
has already been a concluded right which had been created in favour
of the petitioner by determining him as to the highest bidders; since
there was already a sale letter executed in his favour; the terms of
which, has not been complied with by him, the issue would fall to be
within the ambit of Clause 38 of the General Conditions of the
Contract and, hence, the dispute between the employer and the
petitioner / contractor would be referable to the Arbitrator in terms of
Clause 38. Since the petitioner has an agreed /consented, remedy
under the Arbitration Act, the Writ Petition under Article 226 of the
Constitution of India, which when particularly requires a factual
determination of evidence as to what extent the petitioner has

6
complied with the terms of the sale letter, which has been issued to the
petitioner, cannot be subjected to a writ jurisdiction under Article 226
of the Constitution of India.
11. Hence, the Writ Petition is dismissed, with the liberty left
open to the petitioner to seek a reference of a dispute to the arbitrator
under Clause 38 of the General Conditions of the contract.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 24.09.2021
Shiv
